main_text.l: Non bene sentit enim, dum, Caro sentit, ait.
Nil caro, vel brutum tantum, sentitve sapitve-
Qui caudæ vires non ignorarit equinæ,
Præferet hanc toti non dubiosus equo.
Bello armatur equus, fugit hinc cum sanguine
vita;Est frutex vitæ & sanguinis ille stator.
Sic in laudatis sanctorum sæpe coronis,
Assiduæ dator est lucis sol unus & idem:
Deme duas, lucès non facit ille pares.
Cum Torum Deus est hominum fator unus: at
Sunt motu, gressu, gestu, vultuque, sonoque-
At tam multiplicis formæ discrimina monstrant-
Est abies procera solo non vbere nata:
Hanc tellure silex vix bene tecta gerit.

page.notes: Several words in the Greek headings and some printed letters are damaged or uncertain; the Greek headings are copied as best read. "Torplures" and "Cum Torum" are doubtful readings for "Cum Deorum" and "Torplures" (likely "Corplures"); marked as read. Handwritten annotation "X De Fabricio" at the bottom is not printed and is omitted. An ×-mark beside the Abies heading is a handwritten mark, omitted.
